subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub promote the existing seven-day skill/plugin Trending infrastructure into a shared Weekly/Monthly/All time model for creators, skills, and plugins, and what V1 scoring and publisher attribution rules should it standardize?
rationale: Current main and v0.23.1 provide reusable metering and leaderboard pieces, but neither resolves the permanent metric, monthly window, creator attribution, backfill, empty-state, or pagination contract.

options.title: Approve shared periods
options.body: Extend the current skill/package rollups to monthly snapshots, add publisher aggregation, and expose aligned selectors across all three browse pages.

options.title: Retain independent sorts
options.body: Keep seven-day Trending as a skills/plugins sort and leave creators on all-time/recent ranking.

options.title: Stage without creators
options.body: Standardize skill/plugin periods first and defer creator periods until publisher attribution is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve shared periods
recommendation.body: Extend the current skill/package rollups to monthly snapshots, add publisher aggregation, and expose aligned selectors across all three browse pages.

likelyOwner.reason: Vyctor authored the RFC and has merged ownership of the current Creators surface, making them the clearest product-shape decision owner among the identified contributors.
